start.npcText: Don't touch the bench, half of it's drying. Wynne Alder. If you're bleeding, sit. If you're not, talk while I work.

not_bleeding.npcText: Good. Come back when you are — and you will be, if you're going out past the ridge like every young thing with a name to make. Bring me the wound before it's three days old and I'll not have to be interesting about it.

interesting_how.npcText: Interesting is what I call it when the simple thing won't work anymore. Nobody wants to be an interesting case. Ask the reeve about his thumb sometime — go on, ask him, he'll show you before you finish the question.

making.npcText: Fever draught, mostly, while the willow's still good. And a salve for Hedda's forearms that she'll take and not use. Tomas brings me the bark on his way back from the wood, so I get the inner strips and not the rubbish.

responses.text: Do you sell any of it?

sell_it.npcText: Tilda sells the potions. I make the draughts and give them away, which Tilda regards as unfair competition and I regard as the whole point of a village. We've had the argument. It's a good argument, we keep it going.

give_away.npcText: To this village, yes. Twenty households owe me nothing and I owe them my whole life — Serrel's family fed us the winter Elin was born and I have never once been asked about it. That's the ledger I keep and it balances fine.

midwife.npcText: Every child in Hollowbrook under twenty came through my hands, bar the Thatchers' youngest who arrived in a hayloft while I was on the wrong side of the brook. Meg has never let me forget it and never once been unkind about it, which is Meg.

responses.text: Every child? That's most of the village.

most_of_village.npcText: Thirty-one of them, and I could tell you the weather on every one of those days. It's why I don't leave. Ivo writes the years down and I remember them, and between us not much gets lost.

responses.text: Between the two of you, nothing does.

the_hayloft.npcText: Bett Thatcher, four years old now and afraid of nothing, which I put down entirely to the hayloft. Bryn still can't tell the story without sitting down first.

responses.text: Ha. I'll ask him to tell it.
